note: Jasper County Conservation Board's modern campground (opened 2024) at Mariposa Recreation Area NE of Newton, on a ridge above two retention ponds; Mariposa Lake (18 acres, fishing, kayak lockers) lies about 250-400 m east. Primitive Mariposa loop and the Coneflower Cottage are nearby. Back-in sites 1-8 are 60 ft, pull-throughs 9-15 are 40-50 ft. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: 15 water/electric sites, $25 + $4 fee, 2-night minimum, 14-day limit, showers, dump; season added (closes Nov 1, reopens in April). Waterfront downgrade lead (lakeview -> not waterfront): the lake is 250-400 m off behind ponds and a treed shore; no official photo shows it.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (down, lakeview -> not waterfront): Mariposa Lake is 18 acres ('A newly renovated 18-acre lake'), so over the 5-acre line, and every site page says the sites overlook 'Mariposa Lake and two retention ponds'. But on Esri imagery the lake's nearest shore is about 250 m from the east end of the pull-through row and 350-400 m from the ridgetop back-ins, with the larger retention pond (about 1.5 ha, under the 5-acre line) and a treed strip along the lake's west shore between. The ridgetop is about 18-20 m above the lake (DEM 290-292 m vs 272 m), which a 10-15 m shore treeline at about 330 m would still hide. None of the county's eight campground photos shows the lake: they look over fields and woods. The ponds have no value. Unsure after every source, so down.
